title: Comparative Datasets in Multilingual NMT
query: Compare the training and evaluation datasets used in Paper [1] and Paper [2] into a structured comparison table!
ground_truth: Paper [1] experiments on Europarl and MultiUN datasets. Paper [2] experiments on the IITB English-Hindi parallel corpus and the ILCI multilingual parallel corpus.

title: Comparative Baselines in Multilingual Machine Translation
query: Compare the baseline translation approaches and configurations evaluated between Paper [1] and Paper [2]!
ground_truth: Paper [1] compares with pivot-based baselines ('pivoting' and 'pivoting_m') and standard multilingual NMT. Paper [2] compares non-preordered baselines against generic pre-ordering rules and Hindi-tuned pre-ordering rules (CFILT-preorder).

title: Comparative Baseline NER Models across Armenian and Spanish Clinical Domains
query: Compare the baseline algorithms and models evaluated between Paper [1] and Paper [2] for named entity recognition!
ground_truth: Paper [1] evaluates Stanford NER, spaCy 2.0, and a recurrent neural network with a CRF layer. Paper [2] evaluates regular expressions/dictionary look-up, CRF (sklearn-crfsuite), and spaCy NER model alongside BERT.

title: Comparative Datasets across Chinese, Armenian, and Multilingual NER
query: Compare the language corpora and datasets evaluated across Paper [1], Paper [2], and Paper [3]!
ground_truth: Paper [1] uses news sentences from ilur.am for Armenian NER (pioNER). Paper [2] evaluates on Chinese Dialog (DL-PS) and E-commerce (EC-MT, EC-UQ) datasets. Paper [3] evaluates on CoNLL03 (English, German, Spanish, Dutch) and Chinese Weibo and Resume datasets.

title: Comparative KBQA Benchmarks
query: Compare the benchmark datasets on which state-of-the-art results are evaluated in Paper [1] and Paper [2]!
ground_truth: Paper [1] evaluates and achieves state-of-the-art on SimpleQuestions and WebQSP. Paper [2] evaluates on WebQuestions and SimpleQuestions.

title: Comparative Social Media Analysis: Dogmatism vs Rumor Detection
query: Compare the predictive models, target phenomena, and data platforms between Paper [1] and Paper [2]!
ground_truth: Paper [1] builds a logistic regression model to predict dogmatism in Reddit posts across politics, business, science, and AskReddit. Paper [2] detects rumors on Chinese social media (Weibo) using novelty detection and similarity to previously detected rumors.

title: Comparative Word Representations & Semantic Embeddings
query: Compare the core experimental objectives and representation techniques between Paper [1] and Paper [2]!
ground_truth: Paper [1] tests context-specificity in upper layers of ELMo, BERT, and GPT-2 using self-similarity, intra-sentence similarity, and principal component static embeddings. Paper [2] discovers gender associations and coherent word clusters via K-means clustering and WordNet distance concept labeling.

title: Comparative Evaluation Metrics: Rumors vs Non-Collaborative Dialog
query: Compare the evaluation metrics and experimental criteria reported between Paper [1] and Paper [2]!
ground_truth: Paper [1] evaluates accuracy, Detection Error Trade-off (DET) curves, and throughput per second. Paper [2] evaluates perplexity, BLEU, dialog success rate, turn count, and human ratings (quality and fluency).

title: Comparative Baseline Models: Topic Models vs Event Detection
query: Compare the baseline architectures compared against between Paper [1] and Paper [2]!
ground_truth: Paper [1] compares with LDA, Doc-NADE, HTMM, and GMNTM. Paper [2] compares with a cascade of two SVM classifiers (one for detection and one for classification).

title: Comparative Language Scope across Three Papers
query: Compare the languages explored and evaluated across Paper [1], Paper [2], and Paper [3]!
ground_truth: Paper [1] explores German, English, French, Spanish, Romanian, Arabic, and Russian. Paper [2] explores English to Hindi (parent) and Bengali, Gujarati, Marathi, Malayalam, and Tamil (child). Paper [3] evaluates on Spanish clinical reports.

title: Distractor Test: Word Order Divergence Mitigation
query: Which of the two papers addresses word order divergence in translation, and what specific method is proposed?
ground_truth: Only Paper [2] addresses word order divergence, proposing to pre-order assisting language sentences to match the target language word order using generic and Hindi-tuned rules. Paper [1] focuses on cross-lingual pre-training and zero-shot transfer without addressing word order divergence.

title: Distractor Test: Crowdsourcing in Named Entity Recognition
query: Between Paper [1] and Paper [2], which paper uses a crowdsourcing platform or crowd annotators, and who performs the annotations?
ground_truth: Paper [1] did not use crowdsourcing (authors manually annotated the news data). In contrast, Paper [2] utilizes crowd annotations, hiring undergraduate students for Dialog and E-commerce data.

title: Comparative Analysis: Outperforming State-of-the-Art
query: Do the models proposed in Paper [1] and Paper [2] outperform current state-of-the-art architectures across all evaluated tasks?
ground_truth: Neither model achieves unconditional state-of-the-art across all benchmarks. In Paper [1] (TENER), the model does not outperform BERT-based state-of-the-art NER models. In Paper [2], BERT does not reach the best performance across all algorithms compared (e.g. NLNDE scores higher on strict detection).

title: Comparative Dataset Sizes across Dialog and Gender Corpora
query: Compare the reported dataset sizes (number of dialogs, turns, or sentences) between Paper [1] and Paper [2]!
ground_truth: Paper [1] (ANTISCAM) contains 220 dialogs, with 3,044 sentences in the 100 annotated dialog subset. Paper [2] introduces two corpora with over 300,000 (300K) sentences each.

title: Comparative Structural and Typographic Annotation Layers
query: Compare the text structural and typographical information layers extracted between Paper [1] and Paper [2]!
ground_truth: Paper [1] annotates text structure (paragraph, line, and physical page segmentation) and typography (font type, font style bold/italics, and position). Paper [2] focuses on linguistic and semantic event detection using sequence-to-sequence BIO scheme without typography or page layout layers.
